data.title: Accendra Health Faces NYSE Delisting Risk as Stock Price, Market Cap Fall Below Compliance Thresholds
data.description:
Accendra Health Inc (ACH) has disclosed a new risk, in the Share Price & Shareholder Rights category.

Accendra Health Inc. faces heightened listing risk as its common stock has fallen below the NYSE’s minimum price and market capitalization thresholds, triggering formal noncompliance notices and remediation timelines. The company’s reliance on a shareholder-approved reverse split and an NYSE-monitored business plan introduces execution and governance uncertainty that could impede a successful cure.

Should Accendra Health Inc. fail to regain compliance, potential NYSE delisting would likely shift trading to the over-the-counter market, materially reducing share liquidity and investor access. Such an outcome could constrain capital-raising options and exacerbate existing financial pressures from lost Payor contracts and recent business divestitures, negatively affecting operations and cash flows.

Overall, Wall Street has a Hold consensus rating on ACH stock based on 1 Sell and 4 Holds.

data.title: Raízen Approves Restructuring-Linked Capital Increase Up to R$39.8 Billion
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Raizen SA ( (BR:RAIZ55) ).

Raízen’s board approved a private capital increase ranging from R$3.5 billion to R$39.8 billion at R$0.25 per share, making the transaction a condition for its extrajudicial restructuring plan. Shell will provide up to R$3.5 billion, while creditors may exchange eligible claims for shares and other shareholders retain preemptive rights.

Cash proceeds will support working capital and, above specified thresholds, direct 70% toward debt repayment or amortization and 30% toward working capital. The company also approved Units and a Level I ADS program, plus secured debentures for certain creditors, strengthening its restructuring framework while potentially diluting shareholders who do not participate.

data.title: Adex Mining Adjourns Mount Pleasant Appeal to March 2027
data.description:
An announcement from Adex Mining ( (TSE:ADE) ) is now available.

Adex Mining is a Canadian junior mining company focused on the Mount Pleasant multi-metal project in New Brunswick. The property contains tungsten-molybdenum and tin-indium-zinc mineralization, and the company’s shares trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the symbol ADE.

Adex Minerals, the company’s wholly owned subsidiary, and New Brunswick’s Mining Recorder jointly adjourned an appeal hearing from December 2026 to March 11–12, 2027. The appeal challenges the cancellation of a mineral claim over insufficient work expenditures, while an interim stay has reinstated the claim pending a final decision.

The adjournment allows Adex to direct internal resources toward its strategic review and potential transactions involving Mount Pleasant. The company said the delay does not represent a concession and that its independent special committee remains engaged with advisers and interested parties.

data.title: Banca Profilo Sees Early Recovery Amid Repositioning
data.description:
An update from Banca Profilo SPA ( (IT:PRO) ) is now available.

Banca Profilo reported early signs of commercial recovery in the third quarter, with Private Banking assets stabilizing and indirect deposits rising by about €59 million from June. However, nine-month consolidated net revenue fell 36.4% year on year to €32.2 million, while net profit was negative at €2.3 million amid the bank’s reorganization and repositioning.

Digital Banking continued to expand, generating €2.8 million in revenue, up 227.3% year on year, while quarterly net interest income rose 22.3% to €6.0 million. Cost reductions, new partnerships including Athora Italia, strengthened management and hiring across key areas supported the integrated wealth-management strategy, alongside robust capital and liquidity ratios.

data.title: Colombia’s Producer Inflation Surges Past Expectations
data.description:
Colombia’s Producer Price Index rose to 4.54% year over year from 2.20% previously, an increase of 2.34 percentage points, or about 106%. The reading signals a sharp acceleration in producer-price inflation.

The result exceeded the 2.90% analyst estimate by 1.64 percentage points, or roughly 57%. The upside surprise is likely to weigh on rate-sensitive stocks and companies exposed to higher input costs, while reinforcing expectations for tighter monetary policy and creating near-term market pressure.
